newsitem.title: USA: Two senators expect U.S. military action on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Two senators expect U.S. military action on Iraq.

text.p: Two members of the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee said on Monday they expected U.S. military action in response to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's troop movements into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq.
The senators, interviewed on CNN's "Larry King Live" after being briefed by the White House, said they expected the U.S. response would come even without widespread support from U.S. allies.

"No administration, no Pentagon official wants to telegraph what punch if any is going to come, but I think in all likelihood there will be some sort of military response," said Sen. William Cohen, a Maine Republican.
"I would think it would come in the nature of some attack on command-and-control facilities closer to Baghdad rather than in the Kurdish areas," said Cohen on CNN's "Larry King Live."
Sen. Joseph Lieberman, a Democrat from Connecticut, said "there will be a response" but said officials had to be cautious in speaking ahead of any attacks so as not to endanger U.S. forces.
"What it will be, where it will be, time will tell," he said.
"The feeling at the White House ... is quite strong if you let Saddam get away with this he'll keep on going. This is another test and anytime we don't meet his tests we pay for it," Lieberman said."
The United States said on Monday Iraqi troops appeared to be moving deeper into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq, and Clinton had readied a "course of action" in response.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry refused to confirm that Clinton had signed off on military action, but he said that "clearly political, economic and nilitary aspects have been under consideration."
